item.name: Hermes observable-behavior parity closure and upstream drift gate
item.contract: A strict, fail-closed gate determines whether Gormes matches observable Hermes behavior at the latest fetched upstream origin/main SHA. The always-upstream policy records one immutable SHA per pass, advances the checkout and evidence to that SHA, and refuses a parity claim against any older baseline. It ties nested source behaviors to Go implementation and deterministic scenario tests; mapping, row completion, weak-only checks, and Gormes-only tests alone are not parity proof.
item.degraded_mode: If the upstream checkout is unavailable, its SHA differs from the audited baseline, an inventory is stale, or required tests cannot run, report unverified and fail the full-parity claim; never silently accept a partial report.
item.fixture: webpages/docs/parity-evidence/HERMES-BEHAVIOR-ATOMS.md; internal/planning/progress/repoctl/inventory/hermes_contract_inventory_test.go; Hermes fixtures translated to shared deterministic contract fixtures
source_refs: https://github.com/MichaelKinsy/PiG/blob/main/PORT_MAP.md (verification-gate technique only; Hermes remains the compatibility contract)
https://github.com/MichaelKinsy/PiG/blob/main/parity/coverage.md (evidence-grading technique only; do not copy static coverage percentages)
ready_when: The in-repo Hermes checkout and recorded evidence are advanced to the latest fetched origin/main SHA, and that exact SHA is recorded in the source-pairs manifest and inventory.
The behavior-atom inventory and nested source/test inventory have been reconciled against that revision; unresolved implementation atoms remain linked to canonical progress.json rows.
The gate distinguishes strict parity from mapping completeness and Gormes-owned divergences.

A source diff from the audited Hermes SHA to current origin/main has a deterministic report that classifies each added, modified, or deleted path as mapped behavior, mapped tests, or a justified non-runtime exclusion.
The scenario evidence format records source behavior, Go target, test/scenario ID, exact Hermes SHA, command, exit result, and whether the assertion proves an observable contract.
The gate has an explicit record shape for intentional divergences and for source-backed async/concurrency contracts where those affect observable behavior.
not_ready_when: The report passes while any public behavior is partial, missing, unknown, stale, or unmapped.
A source-class match, completed progress row, or Gormes-only unit test is treated as proof without a behavior-asserting scenario.
A behavior-changing divergence or excluded public feature is counted as strict 1:1 parity, or a divergence lacks its observable delta and removal condition.
The gate requires live credentials/services, silently skips unavailable evidence, leaves upstream deltas unresolved, or counts not-run evidence as complete.
An observable async/concurrency behavior has no review of ordering, cancellation, error propagation, ownership, or persistence effects where relevant.
The gate uses a cached or pinned baseline that is older than the latest fetched origin/main.
unblocks: Advance Hermes checkout and source pairs to latest upstream
Classify the upstream delta by feature family
Plan round 2: split upstream delta into builder rows
acceptance: The report records the exact audited Hermes SHA and emits an upstream delta from that SHA to current origin/main; every added, modified, or deleted path has a source-backed disposition, and any unresolved path or revision mismatch fails closed.
The report emits per-status behavior counts and exact unmapped/stale entries, while keeping source-map completeness separate from behavioral verification.

Each behavior claimed as verified links exact Hermes source/test refs to a Go target and deterministic scenario/test ID whose assertions cover observable output, state, ordering, or errors; report evidence grades distinguish mapped-only, weak-only, scenario-verified, and untested, and weak-only or not-run evidence never satisfies strict coverage.

For upstream async/concurrent behavior with observable effects, the contract and tests cover relevant ordering, cancellation, error propagation, concurrency/ownership, and session or persistence effects; any not-applicable dimension has a source-backed rationale.

Each intentional divergence records its rationale, exact observable delta, affected scope, test/evidence, reviewer, and removal condition; any behavior-changing divergence or excluded public Hermes behavior prevents a full 1:1 parity result.
Critical boundary fixtures compare normalized CLI/config output, tool schemas/results, provider request/stream events, persistence/session state, and gateway channel events without live credentials.

A negative fixture using the current unresolved inventory fails; a fully reconciled fixture for one fixed SHA passes only when every strict exit condition is met and no public behavior remains partial, missing, unknown, stale, unmapped, weak-only, or untested.

The final report distinguishes mapping-complete, implementation-incomplete, strict-parity-complete, and unverified; it records the SHA, delta dispositions, evidence counts, divergences, commands and exit results. Missing sources or not-run required evidence produce unverified, never complete.
The gate fails with baseline_stale when the recorded baseline SHA is not the latest fetched origin/main, and fails with baseline_unverified when origin/main cannot be resolved.
item.note: Always-upstream policy accepted by the owner. The executed planning-time baseline is 197f16a12b098f1ea541bbd0a5ddd7d66f2d2dee, 17,230 commits ahead of the previous d0288be5b baseline. The hermes-agent gitlink, source-pairs manifest, and contract inventory now agree on that SHA; source-pair validation passes. The regenerated inventory reports 17,199 unmapped upstream files and 17,209 strict failures, so the strict claim remains unverified. The rolling gate, delta classification, and round-2 planner rows remain open. The rolling freshness gate is now implemented: gormes-repo hermes-contract-inventory --strict --require-latest matches the recorded 197f16a12b baseline and fails closed on drift; strict parity remains unverified with 17,209 unresolved items.
done_signal: The strict gate rejects any baseline older than the latest fetched origin/main, accepts only a fully reconciled latest-SHA inventory with scenario evidence, and records the exact SHA, delta dispositions, evidence grades, and command results.

item.name: Rolling upstream baseline freshness gate
item.contract: Implement the always-upstream freshness step for the strict parity gate. The gate reads the recorded baseline SHA, resolves the latest fetched NousResearch/hermes-agent origin/main, and fails closed when they differ. A matching baseline proceeds to behavior evaluation and emits the source delta from the recorded SHA to origin/main.
item.degraded_mode: A missing or unreachable origin/main, a missing recorded SHA, or a revision-resolution error produces baseline_unverified and no parity claim. A stale baseline produces baseline_stale and no parity claim.
ready_when: The source-pairs manifest and contract inventory both carry an explicit baseline SHA.
The gate can resolve origin/main through an injected git revision function.
The failure evidence codes baseline_stale, baseline_unverified, and baseline_match are defined.
not_ready_when: The gate passes when the recorded SHA differs from origin/main.
The gate silently skips an unreachable or missing origin/main.
The gate emits no delta from the recorded SHA to origin/main.
unblocks: Classify the upstream delta by feature family
Plan round 2: split upstream delta into builder rows
acceptance: TestBaselineFreshnessRejectsStale records a SHA older than origin/main and exits non-zero with baseline_stale plus both SHAs.
TestBaselineFreshnessAcceptsLatest records the origin/main SHA and passes the freshness step with baseline_match.
TestBaselineFreshnessFailsClosedOnUnresolvableOrigin records a revision error and returns baseline_unverified without a parity claim.
TestBaselineDeltaListsChangedPaths emits the added, modified, and deleted paths from the recorded SHA to origin/main.
item.note: Complete 2026-11-02. Added RequireLatest, OriginRevision, and BaselineDelta to the fidelity report, passed them through the contract inventory, and added --require-latest to gormes-repo. The gate emits baseline_match, baseline_stale, or baseline_unverified plus the recorded/latest SHAs and the added/modified/deleted path delta. Tests cover stale, matching, and unverifiable baselines. The live gate matches at 197f16a12b; strict parity still fails with 17,209 unresolved items, which is the expected implementation gap.
done_signal: The gate rejects a stale or unverifiable baseline with baseline_stale/baseline_unverified, accepts a matching latest baseline with baseline_match, and emits the recorded/latest SHAs and delta.

item.name: Gormes update release planner and dry-run contract
item.contract: `gormes update` must distinguish normal release-installed operators from managed source checkouts before it mutates anything. For release installs, the command plans against trusted GitHub Releases: detect install layout, current version/build, OS/arch artifact name, channel policy (`stable` by default, `development` explicit), latest release metadata, snapshot path, components to update, blocked reasons, and whether an update is available. `gormes update --dry-run` prints the exact non-mutating plan; `gormes update --check` performs no mutation and exits 0 when current, 10 when an update is available, and nonzero for check errors. Existing source-checkout behavior from `Self-update command lifecycle safety` remains the managed/dev path and must not be silently used for release installs.
item.degraded_mode: Unknown install layout, unsupported OS/arch, missing release metadata, channel mismatch, dirty unmanaged source checkout, and network/API lookup failures produce typed plan blockers without changing binaries, assets, skills, services, config, credentials, sessions, memory, or source checkouts.

`gormes update --dry-run` prints current version/build, target version/build, source (`github_release` or `managed_source`), channel, artifact, snapshot path, component plan, and blockers without mutation.
`gormes update --check` exits 0 when current, 10 when an update is available, and nonzero for check errors, with JSON and text reports carrying the same state.

Stable vs development channel policy is explicit; release installs use GitHub Releases by default, managed source/dev installs use the existing source lifecycle only when detected or explicitly requested.
No binary, asset, skill, service, config, credential, session, memory, git checkout, or update ledger file changes during planner/check/dry-run tests.
